titel: Star Trek: 60 years to the most gloriously nerdy enterprise

einzeiler: Celebrating six decades of Star Trek, its Jewish roots, and classic episodes.
kurzfassung: Amanda Borschel-Dahn and guest Jordan Hoffman celebrate the 60th anniversary of Star Trek by exploring the franchise's deep Jewish connections, behind-the-scenes stories, and cultural legacy. They review two specific episodes: the original series classic 'The City on the Edge of Forever' and Deep Space Nine's 'In the Hands of the Prophets.' Finally, they tease a review of Gal Gadot's upcoming action film 'The Runner' for the next episode.
stichpunkte: Jordan Hoffman and Amanda Borschel-Dahn discuss the 60th anniversary of the first Star Trek broadcast.
The hosts explore the strong Jewish representation among Star Trek's cast, writers, and producers.
Hoffman shares an eccentric personal dinner story involving legendary sci-fi writer Harlan Ellison.
They debate Gene Roddenberry's complicated legacy, worldview, and controversial remarks.
Borschel-Dahn shares her perspective on watching the original series episode 'The City on the Edge of Forever' for the first time.
They analyze the Deep Space Nine episode 'In the Hands of the Prophets' and its themes of orthodoxy versus science.
The episode concludes with a preview of next week's review of the Gal Gadot film 'The Runner'.

kapitel.titel: Reviewing The City on the Edge of Forever

clips.hook: The surprising truth about the very first Star Trek broadcast
clips.text: The first broadcast of the series did not feature the pilot episode that was filmed initially, nor was it the first episode produced for the regular season.

clips.hook: A sci-fi legend whose favorite hobby was litigation
clips.text: The prominent science fiction writer had a distinct personal habit of constantly filing lawsuits against people for thrills.

clips.hook: The unexpected synagogue origin of a famous sci-fi hand gesture
clips.text: The iconic Vulcan greeting was adapted from a specific ritual hand movement observed during synagogue services in childhood.

clips.hook: The ultimate ethical dilemma of time travel
clips.text: Captain Kirk faces a painful dilemma when he discovers that saving the woman he loves will inadvertently lead to a Nazi victory on Earth.

clips.hook: Strategic wardrobe choices in modern action cinema
clips.text: The premise of an upcoming thriller revolves entirely around the lead actress running through the entire narrative in tight athletic wear.

beschreibung:
Welcome to The Reel Schmooze with ToI film reviewer Jordan Hoffman and host Amanda Borschel-Dan, where we bring you all the entertainment news and film reviews a Jew can use.
This month marks the 60th anniversary of the pioneering sci-fi series, Star Trek. Expert in all things Trekky, Hoffman, when he's not schmoozing with Borschel-Dan, also hosts the STARLOG podcast and co-wrote The Star Trek Book of Friendship.
So this week, the duo nerd out on all things Jewish behind the beloved franchise -- Spock's famous hand gesture is adapted from the Priestly Blessing, in one notable example. Eventually, we laser in on two episodes that illustrate the show's ethos.
From the original Star Trek television series, Hoffman chose "The City on the Edge of Forever." We hear about how, when time-traveling to 1930s New York, Captain Kirk and Mr. Spock faced a tough decision to stave off a potential global Nazi takeover.
And in Deep Space Nine's "In the Hands of the Prophets," we see how the program deals with themes of religious extremism versus science.
Let’s hear who gave this series an “oy,” “meh” or the prized “not bad” this week on The Reel Schmooze.
The Reel Schmooze is produced by Ari Schlacht and can be found wherever you get your podcasts.
